nodes.label: Flame.vert
nodes.rationale: Vertex shader for the torch flame body: places three flat camera-facing billboard cards in flame-local space and applies the CPU-driven envelopes; all the look lives in the fragment shader.

nodes.label: CPU-built camera-facing billboard basis
nodes.rationale: mvpMat is built CPU-side from the camera's own right/up/forward vectors because a billboard must face the camera and cannot ride the torch's orientation; the shader just multiplies by it.

nodes.label: Silhouette punched per-pixel, not by mesh
nodes.rationale: The mesh is a flat card and the flame's outline is discarded out per pixel in Flame.frag, which is what lets the flame fray at the edges and let wisps detach from the body.

nodes.label: Three depth-offset flame cards
nodes.rationale: Cards are separated along local z by 0.10 units and given varying width/height (far larger, near smaller) so the stack reads as a convex volume with parallax rather than one flat sheet.

nodes.label: Reusing the main pass's global descriptor set
nodes.rationale: The flame binds the very same DSglobal set 0 as the main pass so it never needs its own copy of eyePos/lightCount kept in step, even though it only reads time.

nodes.label: FlameUniformBufferObject (set 1, per torch)
nodes.rationale: One small per-torch block: billboard mvpMat, per-torch seed, brightness intensity, lean, heightScale, glareBoost and target color.

nodes.label: Separate brightness and height envelopes
nodes.rationale: intensity (~0.30..1.40, spring-smoothed) and heightScale (~0.78..1.09, chased far more slowly) are kept separate because light output can flicker fast while flame height follows the fuel column and lags it.

nodes.label: Quadratic (h*h) lean from hand motion
nodes.rationale: The CPU derives a billboard-local lean from hand motion; applying it as lean*h*h pins the base and swings the tip, concentrating sway where a real flame's is.
